claims.claim_text: The indexed Miyoji Oda is a high-confidence match to the Miyoji Oda documented in a wartime War Relocation Authority roster and a later Los Angeles Times obituary.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name is corroborated across the OSS index, a wartime roster, and an obituary; the roster and obituary independently name the same siblings Frank, Kazume, and Lillian.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name and three matching sibling identifiers across two independent reputable sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The roster documents Miyoji Oda, age 19, in a wartime relocation-center household. It does not identify an employer or establish the immediate transition into OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The project records the identity context without treating confinement, residence, or family association as employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Gabriel Odalovich is probably the World War II Army first lieutenant documented in a Veterans Affairs-derived national-cemetery transcription.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The unusual exact name and Army lieutenant status agree; the derivative burial record supplies a birth date and cemetery locator but no OSS or employment evidence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable, not settled: an unusual exact name and compatible rank agree, but no protected identifier or direct OSS linkage is available in the accessible source.
claims.temporal_assessment: The burial transcription establishes World War II Army service only; it does not establish a pre-OSS employer or immediate assignment.
claims.match_notes: This qualified identity should be tested against Box 568 before elevation to high confidence.
